name: microphone
summary: One wireless handheld microphone, held in one hand. No cord, no stand, no second microphone.

draw.shape: A handheld stick microphone: a rounded mesh grille head above a straight tapered barrel, roughly the length of the character's own hand plus half again. The grille is the widest part and reads as a distinct ball against the barrel.
draw.material: Brushed metal barrel with a darker mesh grille, lightly specular.
draw.readability: Drawn in full and clearly readable in every frame, never a smudge, a stub, or a shape that merges into the costume behind it.

hands.character-right: The fist wraps the barrel below the grille, fingers closed around it, thumb along the side. The grille end always leads.

hold.orientation: The grille end faces the mouth. Raised, it points up and inward toward the face; lowered, it stays head-up with the grille still the leading end. It never points away from the character, and never reads upside down.
hold.rest: At the upper torso, grille up, unless the set below or the brief says otherwise.

carriage.dance: The microphone does not need to point at the face. The prop hand and arm are free to move with the dance, the grille still leading.
carriage.sing: Brought toward the mouth for the sustained phrase, grille to the lips, kept readable against the face rather than covering it.
carriage.flinch: Stays controlled at the upper torso through the reaction.
carriage.guard: Kept upright in the prop hand while the free arm shields the torso.
carriage.entrance: Lifted once in acknowledgement, then settled at the upper torso.
carriage.victory: Raised with the celebration, still upright, grille up.
carriage.ko: Lowers to hang loosely at the side, still in the prop hand, grille still up.

never: in the character-left hand, or swapped between hands across a set
a cord, cable or microphone stand
replaced by a bare fist, an open hand or an empty hand in any frame, whatever the arm is doing
held by the grille, or pointed away from the character
